The segment from P_j to the displaced peak crosses P_1P_l at Q_0 in both relative interiors, proving an actual quadrilateral for every ε>0. Its ear altitude is ε/k_0 times the old altitude, giving area ε. The two affected margins strictly increase from nonnegative base values because both were negative at P_j. The unaffected margin stays negative throughout the ear because it is negative at the old base and positive at P_j.

The negative-corner clipping and coarea formulas at zero ear area give the two affected derivatives exactly. Their denominators L²(1−θ) and H²θ stay positive on the closed interval. The moving peak heights enter multiplied by the ear area, which vanishes at zero, so no moving-height term is missing from the first derivatives. Affected old and ear sections intersect only at one old-edge point and their lengths add.
